fixes.explanation: False is right, baker. The baby pulled his hand back and his brother came out (Genesis 38:29). Then his brother came out with the scarlet thread around his wrist (Genesis 38:30). So the twin with the thread was born second. He stuck his hand out first and still lost the race, and that's a rough day at the starting line.

I think Hirah would love to say otherwise, friend. But Genesis 38:20 says Judah sent him with the young goat to collect the items he had left with the woman, and he could not find her. He's got a goat, an errand and nobody to hand it to. That's an awkward spot to be in.

That's exactly what they say, and it's the whole answer. The men of that place tell him, “No shrine prostitute has been here…” (Genesis 38:21) I bet Hirah wished for a different answer, because who wants to carry that news back? He does it anyway, and in verse 22 he tells Judah, “I could not find her…”

problems.problem: It has 6 sentences. Explanations are 3 to 5 sentences.
“That's a long walk home” adds a distance and destination the text does not give. Hirah returns to Judah, but the passage does not say he walks home.
“Nobody at Enaim has seen her” goes beyond what the men say. They say no shrine prostitute has been there; the text does not say nobody saw Tamar.
